instructions-are-always-loaded-skills-ar.header: Instructions are always loaded, skills are not
instructions-are-always-loaded-skills-ar.description: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md “at the start of every session” and loads a skill “on demand” [1]. Codex, Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot document the same split for their instruction files and skills [2]. ChatGPT custom and project instructions were not read, and whether the Gemini app loads its instructions at the start of each session is unverified, so the split is not confirmed for those two apps.

skill-vs-agents-md-as-google-puts-it.header: Skill vs. AGENTS.md, as Google puts it
skill-vs-agents-md-as-google-puts-it.description: Day 3 has a “Skill vs. AGENTS.md” passage: “From one side AGENTS.md is always loaded within the project; Skills load on demand. The cleanest setups use both.” It advises keeping AGENTS.md tight and, if needed, using it as a router into the skills library “with a short catalog at the bottom that tells the agent what's available” [1]. Day 1 calls always-loaded rule files static context [2]. Both are Google's vendor guidance on how to split the two, not evidence that the split works.

four-things-in-the-room.title: Four things in the room
four-things-in-the-room.script: Four things shape what the model knows, and they do four different jobs: personal instructions, project instructions, skills and connectors. In the control room they are your notebook, the project brief on the wall, the manual at the console, and the cable to the sonar and the lab database.

read-the-tags.title: Read the tags
read-the-tags.script: Take them one at a time. Personal instructions are static, and they follow you into every project, as your notebook comes with you onto any ship. Project instructions are static too, but only inside this one project. Skills are dynamic, because one arrives when a task needs it, and a connector's results are dynamic too, because they arrive from another system while you work; the connector also lets the model act in that system. That is the split from the last Slide, now with names.

your-words-may-differ.title: Your words may differ
your-words-may-differ.script: Your app may use other words for these four, so match the job, not the word. And if you work with a coding agent, the other view shows the files: your personal instructions file, AGENTS.md for the project, a SKILL.md for each skill, and a server for each connector.
